title: Why a pir or shaykh?
ur: پیر یا شیخ کی ضرورت کیوں؟
summary: If the Qur'an, the hadith and the books of fiqh are in front of us, why give bai'at at anyone's hand? Hazrat's answers: the teacher, the one trusted guide, the power of company, and love for Allah's sake.

blocks.p: Haqeeqat-e-Bai'at writes down the question people ask, and then answers it: the Qur'an, the hadith and the books of fiqh are all in front of us, so why give bai'at at anyone's hand?

blocks.q: Think carefully: two and two make four. Arithmetic is such certain knowledge that hardly any other is so certain. Yet from the first class to the tenth it is learned from teachers, and only then does one master it.

blocks.p: A person cannot see his own mistakes; the teacher keeps catching them. If a teacher is needed in such obvious things and in worldly work, Hazrat reads, then why would a spiritual teacher, a shaykh, not be needed for travelling the path of Allah?
Why stay with one shaykh? Hearing the different views of different people leaves a person bewildered, so one should make a trusted personality one's guide.

blocks.q: Think: if in an important court case a new lawyer were engaged every day, the case could not be pursued properly, nor could success be hoped for.

blocks.h: Istighfar with the one whose heart is lit

blocks.p: Every Muslim should do istighfar, so why is a murshid needed for it? Hazrat answers from the verse of Surah an-Nisa that he reads: asking forgiveness on one's own is not enough; the prayer of one whose heart is enlightened should also be sought. 'Becoming a murid begins with istighfar: the murshid prays for forgiveness for him, and there is hope that it will be accepted.'
Every person's thoughts and company spread around him, like ripples in water. If a big stone and a small pebble are thrown in together, the big stone's ripples swallow the pebble's.

blocks.q: In the same way, a person of ordinary thoughts and weak faith who sits in the company of a perfected one: his doubtful and harmful thoughts grow weaker and weaker.
There is an old saying: 'Whoever has no pir, his pir is Shaytan.' The murid has his master's hand over him, so Shaytan cannot touch him.

blocks.p: Is it necessary for everyone? Hazrat answers: for whoever hates bad things and keeps away from them, is drawn to good, and considers it necessary to keep the rules of the path at a high level. 'If you do not consider it necessary, you are deprived.'
Why does the murid love his murshid? For the sake of Allah. A person is with the one he loves, and the murids are spiritual children.

blocks.q: Who are these murids? Spiritual children. In sha Allah, the murids will be joined with their master; they will rise with him.
